Whether a row the round carried out now asks for another pair

pair_change.Rd

Decided on 2026-11-09: a row the channel has sealed does not change its pair, the instance, the project and the person it was carried out for. Carried out on the new pair, it would leave the old one on the instance with no row to govern it, since the round revokes only what a row asks to revoke; a revoked row moved to another pair would take away an access it never governed. Whoever wrote the change, the owner included, and with an approval or not: the row stops before the plan, nothing is written on the instance, nobody is created, and the row keeps its seal and its owner.

Usage

pair_change(executed, current, target, creating, rewritten, revoked = FALSE)

Arguments

executed

The server, project_id and username carried out: the row as read when its seal did not move, otherwise what log_executed_row() or log_executed_unverified() answered.

current

The row as the register holds it, a list or a one-row data frame with server and project_id.

target

The username the round would now serve, "" when the resolution names nobody or would create somebody.

creating

Whether the round would create a person for the row.

rewritten

Whether a write of the person fields by somebody other than the channel stands in the row since its last execution; NA when the log does not say who wrote it, which counts as a write.

revoked

Whether the row asks for revoked.

Value

A list with code, one of the two codes or "", and changed, which of "server", "project_id" and "person" moved, or "account" for the second code.

Details

Two codes, for the two causes, so that whoever reads the message knows at once what to do:

  • DATO_COPPIA_CAMBIATA, the referent's: server or project_id differ from the values carried out, or somebody wrote the person (first name, last name, contact address) and the round would now serve somebody else, another account or a person to create. Setting the fields back to the values carried out brings the row back as it was; another person or another project is a new request, and this one is revoked, its fields back first;

  • TRASPORTO_IDENTITA_CAMBIATA, for IT, decided on 2026-11-09 as well: the round would serve another account or create one while nobody wrote the person in the row, so the account changed on Entra (renamed, deleted, its name corrected). Nothing in the row explains it, and the referent has nothing to undo.

The pair comes first: it is a change the referent made and can undo, and the account is looked at once it is back.

Who the round would serve is the resolution's to say. A verdict that names nobody, ambiguous or a collision nobody answered, is left to the code of the identity, which concedes nothing either; a person to create is somebody else on a row carried out, whatever name the round would give them. A username carried out the log does not say decides nothing, except against a creation, and nor does an empty one: a revocation closed before anybody was resolved was carried out for nobody.

A revoked row whose person the tenant no longer holds is no change, decided on 2026-11-10, when nobody wrote the person in it: there is nobody to take the access from and nobody to create, and the round closes the row before any instance is asked, as it did before the rule. Stopped for IT, the rows long closed that way would bring an outcome and a copy each on the first round. A revoked row that resolves to another account that exists still stops here: revoking that account would take away an access the row never gave. Since 2026-11-12 the round does not ask this function about a revoked row whose version carried out is certain and whose instance and project did not move, revocation_exits(): it revokes the username carried out instead.
